narrative.overview:
The screen is a work surface at the counter, not a dashboard someone admires. It is read standing up, often on a phone held in one hand, under the flat tube lighting of a hire shop. The ground is paper rather than pure white because a glaring screen is tiring across a nine-hour day; controls are 36px tall because they are finger targets; figures are set in tabular numerals globally because this app is a wall of quantities, money and day counts that have to line up in a column.

The system is deliberately quiet so the few loud things can be heard. One accent colour means press this or you are here. Three status colours mean late, due and settled, and nothing decorative may borrow them. Depth is a step in lightness, never a shadow.

Numbers are the content; everything else is furniture. A screen that makes the reader do arithmetic has failed.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground, ink text, no glare — never pure white, never pure black
One signal colour; three status colours that nothing else may use
Flat surfaces, tonal depth, hairline rules
Finger-sized controls throughout, because the primary device is a phone at a counter
Tabular figures everywhere; monospace reserved for codes checked against a printed label
One loud element per screen, and it is whatever needs a phone call

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Ink Blue appears where a hand should go: the primary button, the active nav item, the focus ring, a link. If it appears twice in the same decision, one of them is wrong. It is never used to tint a surface or to make a section feel branded.

rules.name: The Reserved Status Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and green mean late, due and settled. No chart accent, illustration, hover state or empty-state graphic may use them for any other purpose. A reader must be able to trust that red on this screen means money at risk.

rules.name: The No Pure White Rule
rules.body: The page ground is paper (oklch(0.986 0.002 258)). Pure white is reserved for cards and popovers, where it does the work of lifting a sheet off the page.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on html and is not to be overridden. Every quantity, price and day count is compared down a column, so a 1 and a 7 must occupy the same width.

rules.name: The Mono Is Machine-Readable Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono marks strings a person checks character by character against a printed label — RN-000004, a SKU, a barcode. Monospace is never used to make an ordinary label look technical.

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: Body text is 0.875rem. Inputs render at 1rem on phones so iOS does not zoom the viewport when a field takes focus.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Any action staff perform more than a few times a day must be reachable at the bottom of a phone screen, not in a header.

rules.name: The No Stretched Card Rule
rules.body: A card's height is its content. Where a grid row mixes a long list with a short one, the row aligns to the top; a bordered card with a void inside it reads as broken.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. Depth is a step in lightness, not a lift: sidebar < background < card < popover. A shadow in this app means a true overlay — dialog, dropdown, sheet, tooltip — and nothing else.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A coloured edge on a card, list item or callout is 1px. Thicker coloured bars read as a costume; if an item needs more emphasis than a hairline, it needs a different treatment, not a heavier stroke.

dos: Do make every figure a link to the rows behind it.
Do state a number in the unit the reader is about to act on — units still out, days late, money owed — and make sure the figure beside a label is actually a measure of that label.
Do use the three status colours for status only, and give good news a quiet card.
Do size controls for a finger: 36px minimum height for anything tapped at the counter.
Do keep tabular figures on for every quantity, price and count.
Do separate surfaces with a hairline and a step in lightness.
Do let a card be as tall as its content (items-start on mixed-content grids).
Do distinguish a failed request from an empty one — use ErrorState with a retry, never the empty-state copy.
Do compute anything derived from the reader's clock in the browser, not during SSR.
donts: Don't use Ink Blue as a surface tint, a gradient, or a section background. It marks a hand's destination and nothing else.
Don't put a shadow on an in-page surface. Flat is the rule; shadows mean true overlays.
Don't draw a coloured edge thicker than 1px on a card, list item or callout.
Don't use pure white for the page ground or pure black for text.
Don't use monospace for ordinary labels; it is reserved for codes checked against a label.
Don't plot a sparse server series directly — fill the missing periods so an axis labelled 'the last 30 days' actually spans thirty days.
Don't add a second loud element to a screen that already has one.
